newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Rubin says dollar policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Rubin says dollar policy unchanged.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Monday that U.S. dollar policy was unchanged and declined to comment on whether the United States was considering intervening in foreign exchange markets.
"Our dollar policy has not changed," he said. "As we've said many times, we will not comment on our intentions with respect to what we may do 'til after we've done it," he said.
"We'll act when it's appropriate and not act when it's not appropriate," Rubin added.

He noted that Japanese government officials had expressed concern about recent movements of the yen and that the United States shared those concerns because of the impact the yen's weakness could have on Japan's external trade surplus.
The United States is concerned that a cheaper yen will encourage more imports of Japanese-made goods and worsen the U.S. trade deficit with Japan.
He repeated that Japan should seek domestic demand-led growth and avoid a significant increase in its current account surplus.
Asked whether Japanese authorities had been in contact about possible currency market intervention, Rubin said, "I think I've said as much as I choose to say on the subject."

In response to questions about current budget negotiations between the Clinton administration and Congress, Rubin gave an upbeat assessment, saying that there was "a very good atmosphere" and that it was his opinion that an agreement likely could be reached. However, he declined to speculate when this might occur.
Rubin, while unveiling proposed tax simplification proposals, said any tax cut should not threaten a balanced budget.
